title: Literature watch, assembled
sub: A level-0 watch decides what is new, a level-1 call reads each new item, and code attaches every citation.

nodes.l: Summarize each new item, one call each
Attach each citation from its own record
A person reads it and opens what matters

steps.h: The timer fires: nothing decided anything
steps.d:
A weekly schedule, fixed when the watch was set up.
The sources and the topic were chosen by a person, once,
and nothing in this run changes either

steps.h: Your code queries each source in the list
steps.d:
3 sources, 5 records listed between them
city-open-data-notices returned nothing at all, which is
reported as silence rather than as a quiet week

steps.h: Your code works out which records are new
steps.d:
2 dropped as dated before the last run (09/15/2026)
1 dropped as already reported: the journal version of last
week's preprint, same title, different id
2 new
steps.m: no model call: this is the level-0 half

steps.h: One call per new item, with its title and abstract
steps.d:
2 calls, not 5: the watch half decided what gets read
Each reply is three fields, validated against the schema,
with one retry if it does not parse

steps.h: Your code attaches each citation from the source record
steps.d:
authors, year, title, venue and address, built by _cite
The schema has no field for any of them, so the model has
nowhere to write a citation of its own

2 items with citations, 1 already-reported item named,
1 silent source named
opens the full text of anything they intend to act on
steps.m: read before anything is cited elsewhere
